blocks.v: Spring Branch may not be the first neighborhood that comes to mind for standout Indian food, but Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine is changing that narrative in the best way possible. Despite being a relatively new restaurant, this spot is already poppin’—thanks to its rich flavors, warm hospitality, and authentic South Indian cooking. Everything from the service to the atmosphere feels welcoming, and the food delivers comfort and excitement in equal measure.

The menu highlights traditional favorites prepared with care by South Indian chefs, and the results are incredible: crisp dosas, fragrant biryanis, flavorful chutneys, and satisfying appetizers. With generous portions and bold spices, Ruchi’s offers a dining experience that feels both homey and celebratory. Add lively music videos and travel shows playing in the background, and the whole restaurant buzzes with joy.
Masala Dosa with coconut chutney, sambar & kurma
Veggie samosas with yogurt mint chutney & tamarind chutney
Ras Malai topped with pistachios & dried rose petals

“I don't think this restaurant has even been opened for a year but man it’s poppin’, the flavors, the service, everything. This gem of a spot is located within the Spring Branch area… a part of town that’s typically not known for Indian food. Everything about Ruchi's was perfect. Down to their service, warm environment and tantalizing food. Wow! I asked the Non-Indian servers if the chefs were Indian.. and she said yes.. in fact they are South Indian.
Perfect! No wonder the Masala Dosa hit the spot. Huge, full of savory potato filling and complemented with coconut sambar, kurma, etc.

Biryani was pretty good as well. Full of meat, spices and savory goodness. I was amazed at how much food was left over after everyone ate. The food was so delicious that everyone continued to peck at their plates. We got full quick, generous servings that were packed full of flavor. We also like the appetizers served in the beginning, potato veggie samosas that were complemented with green yogurt chutney and tamarind chutney.

Lastly, we enjoyed the Ras Malai, a sweet cottage cheese dumpling dessert that's soaked in a milky saffron base, topped with crushed pistachios and dried rose flowers. Sweet closing to sum up a warm fun-filled night.
All in all, everyone had a good time at this cute little spot tucked out in S.B. They have TVs with colorful music blasting, as well as food travel shows.
Thanks for the warm service and wonderful hospitality. We will surely revisit next time around, perhaps during lunch while sipping on chai and such!

blocks.v: A Cozy Thursday Evening With Sushi, Fried Rice, Mocktails, and Family Time
"My husband, toddler, a good friend, and I enjoyed a cozy Thursday evening dinner at KIMOTO Premium Sushi All You Can Eat in Houston.

If you’re unfamiliar with the term, AYCE stands for “All You Can Eat,” and KIMOTO offers an extensive menu that allows guests to sample a variety of sushi rolls, sashimi, appetizers, hot dishes, and desserts throughout the meal.

From the moment we walked in, the large restaurant felt vibrant yet inviting. The dark-lit dining room, accented by small floating Japanese-style lamps, created a cozy atmosphere that was perfect for a relaxed weekday evening.

One item that always stands out to me is their chicken fried rice. It has a nice char from the wok, plenty of flavor, and is one of those dishes that appeals to both adults and little ones alike. This is an item that my toddler always enjoys eating and it makes for the perfect item to share around the table.

Among my favorite sushi selections were the Baked Salmon Roll, Houston Roll, and Shibuya Crossing Roll. The Baked Salmon Roll was warm, creamy, and comforting, while the Houston Roll and Shibuya Crossing Roll offered plenty of flavor, spice and variety. I also enjoyed the jalapeño poppers, which had a satisfying tempura crunch and made for a great starter.
Beyond the sushi, we tried the beef bulgogi, a classic Korean beef dish served sizzling on a hot plate. The beef was savory with a slightly sticky glaze that made it a nice complement to the meal.
To accompany dinner, I ordered the Lychee Delight mocktail, a refreshing and bubbly drink with delicate floral notes and a hint of rose. It was light, fragrant, and paired wonderfully with the meal.
For dessert, I finished with their green tea ice cream, which was light, refreshing, and the perfect sweet ending after enjoying so many savory dishes.

What made the evening even more enjoyable was the service. The staff members were friendly, communicative and attentive throughout the meal, helping create an experience that felt welcoming and unrushed.

Overall, KIMOTO is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a quality all-you-can-eat sushi experience in Houston. Between the flavorful fried rice, creative sushi rolls, crispy appetizers, refreshing drinks, and cozy atmosphere, it’s a place I would happily return to for another family dinner or casual night out with friends."

This dinner felt like an easy, cozy weekday outing: the kind of meal where everyone at the table could find something to enjoy. The AYCE format made the evening feel flexible and fun, while the atmosphere kept it relaxed enough for a Thursday night dinner with family and a friend.
The combination of sushi rolls, crispy starters, hot dishes, a refreshing mocktail, and green tea ice cream made the meal feel complete from start to finish.
Sara’s favorite sushi selections were the Baked Salmon Roll, Houston Roll, and Shibuya Crossing Roll.
The Baked Salmon Roll brought a warm, creamy, comforting bite, while the Houston Roll and Shibuya Crossing Roll added more flavor, spice, and variety to the meal.
The jalapeño poppers made a strong impression as a starter. Their tempura crunch gave the meal a crispy, satisfying beginning before the sushi and hot dishes arrived.
The beef bulgogi added a savory, sizzling element to the meal. Served on a hot plate with a slightly sticky glaze, it complemented the sushi and gave the table another layer of flavor.
The Lychee Delight mocktail was light, fragrant, and refreshing, with bubbly floral notes and a hint of rose. It paired well with the variety of savory dishes.
For dessert, the green tea ice cream offered a cool, refreshing finish after a full AYCE meal.
The chicken fried rice was the most family-friendly standout. It had a nice wok char, plenty of flavor, and worked beautifully as a shared dish for both adults and Sara’s toddler.
It is the kind of comforting table item that helps make a sushi dinner easier and more enjoyable when dining with a little one.

“Between the flavorful fried rice, creative sushi rolls, crispy appetizers, refreshing drinks, and cozy atmosphere, it’s a place I would happily return to for another family dinner or casual night out with friends.”

Sara’s visit shows KIMOTO as a strong choice for a Houston AYCE sushi dinner that feels both fun and comfortable. The restaurant works well for families, friends, and casual weekday plans, especially for diners who enjoy variety and want to sample sushi, appetizers, hot dishes, drinks, and dessert in one meal.

From the moment we walked in, the large restaurant felt vibrant yet inviting. The dark-lit dining room, accented by small floating Japanese-style lamps, created a cozy atmosphere that was perfect for a relaxed weekday evening.


One item that always stands out to me is their chicken fried rice. It has a nice char from the wok, plenty of flavor, and is one of those dishes that appeals to both adults and little ones alike. This is an item that my toddler always enjoys eating and it makes for the perfect item to share around the table.


Among my favorite sushi selections were the Baked Salmon Roll, Houston Roll, and Shibuya Crossing Roll. The Baked Salmon Roll was warm, creamy, and comforting, while the Houston Roll and Shibuya Crossing Roll offered plenty of flavor, spice and variety. I also enjoyed the jalapeño poppers, which had a satisfying tempura crunch and made for a great starter.


Beyond the sushi, we tried the beef bulgogi, a classic Korean beef dish served sizzling on a hot plate. The beef was savory with a slightly sticky glaze that made it a nice complement to the meal.


To accompany dinner, I ordered the Lychee Delight mocktail, a refreshing and bubbly drink with delicate floral notes and a hint of rose. It was light, fragrant, and paired wonderfully with the meal.


For dessert, I finished with their green tea ice cream, which was light, refreshing, and the perfect sweet ending after enjoying so many savory dishes.


What made the evening even more enjoyable was the service. The staff members were friendly, communicative and attentive throughout the meal, helping create an experience that felt welcoming and unrushed.


Overall, KIMOTO is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a quality all-you-can-eat sushi experience in Houston. Between the flavorful fried rice, creative sushi rolls, crispy appetizers, refreshing drinks, and cozy atmosphere, it’s a place I would happily return to for another family dinner or casual night out with friends."

This dinner felt like an easy, cozy weekday outing: the kind of meal where everyone at the table could find something to enjoy. The AYCE format made the evening feel flexible and fun, while the atmosphere kept it relaxed enough for a Thursday night dinner with family and a friend.


The combination of sushi rolls, crispy starters, hot dishes, a refreshing mocktail, and green tea ice cream made the meal feel complete from start to finish.

Check out Phoenicia. You'll never want to leave!

“I like this market! It’s a small specialty shop with exclusively Japanese products. Always clean, always organized, and never overly scented. The produce is hit or miss—cilantro was limp, but cherry tomatoes were vibrant. Prices can be a shock, especially for imported dressings and sauces.

The fresh food section was pretty bare when I visited, though I’m not sure I’d buy sushi here anyway. I love their chocolate bourbon biscuits—crisp and very chocolatey—as well as their savory rice crackers. I picked up wasabi ones this time. They carry plenty of ready-to-drink coffees and teas; my favorite is Sangaria Royal Milk Tea, lightly sweet and made with simple ingredients.
This plaza is quiet and tucked away, but worth the stop if you like browsing international markets. Support local!”

Open since June 2023, this compact yet well-stocked beauty kiosk sits just inside the Kohl’s entrance, making it an easy stop during a quick errand run or a dedicated beauty shopping trip.

Despite its smaller footprint, the selection mirrors that of larger Sephora locations: fragrances, lotions, makeup, skincare, and gift items all line the shelves. The space feels airy and relaxed, offering the rare pleasure of browsing beauty products without the usual bustle, perfume cloud, or shoulder bumping typical of busier stores.

Customer service shines here, with friendly greetings, helpful answers, and smooth checkout experiences—including the use of account points and seasonal discounts. Nestled in a growing and vibrant part of West Houston, this location adds a modern, accessible beauty option to the neighborhood.

Located in a thriving Westchase retail corridor

“So this is a new location of Sephora and they have been open since June 2023. Walk inside Kohl's and you'll spot Sephora's fairly decent sized kiosk store to the left side of the store. I can't remember the last time I visited a Kohl's location, but this made for a good walk and fun visit.

I actually like this location! It's smaller compared to their regular stores yet they pretty much have every item that you would find at regular Sephora stores. Lotions, fragrances and gift items? ld.headline: Slim Chickens – A Pearland Visit with Hits, Misses & a Lot of Sauce Potential
ld.description: Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston—often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. blocks.v: Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston—often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. This Pearland visit, however, delivered a mixed experience: a few standout bites, a few letdowns, and a whole lot of room for improvement. While the concept is promising and the menu broad, not everything hit the mark this time around.

The fried mushrooms were the star of the meal—crispy, warm, and full of satisfying texture. Unfortunately, the rest of the plate didn’t follow suit. The tenders lacked crispness, the fries leaned soft rather than crunchy, and the Texas toast was serviceable but unremarkable. The much-hyped Slims sauce, said to resemble Cane’s, leaned more toward creamy tomato soup than tangy dipping bliss, making it a surprise mismatch for the meal. To top it off, the ranch—requested as a backup savior—never made it into the to-go bag.

Still, Slim Chickens offers a wide selection of sandwiches, wraps, and comforting desserts, leaving the door open for a possible revisit at another location. And for dessert lovers, the pudding jars and cheesecake cups may be the hidden gems worth exploring—especially on a hot Texas day.
“Hmm Slim Chickens! More like the bare bones of it. A place that I had high expectations for, but to be honest, those expectations fell flat upon first sight and bite.

I was excited to try this spot and have noticed it in different parts of Houston but happened to be out in the city of Pears and found it out of happenstance. Twas' evening time and the hunger pangs began for a snack. Something not too heavy, but not too light. My initial thoughts were to visit Canes because I was craving their sauce and tenders, but didn't know which side of Pearland it was at. Slims popped up during my excursion and I thought.. well why not? I've seen this spot before so let’s give it a shot.

Ordered their simple meal of tenders that came with fries and texas toast. Also ordered their fried mushrooms as well. The fried mushrooms were bomb! Incredibly warm and crispy. They had good texture and taste. I wish I could say the same for the rest of my meal, but everything else was OK (fries and tenders). The tenders weren't that crispy, maybe because of all that buttermilk batter? They were also a bit small. Fries weren't crispy, mostly soft. Texas toast was buttery and garlicky, it was average in taste.

I was excited to try their Slims sauce, which I was told was similar to Canes. At least that's what the drive thru staff said. With excitement I asked for 2 orders of their Slims sauce. To my surprise, it did not taste anything similar to Canes sauce. Instead it was very creamy and tomato flavored in taste. Almost like a cream of tomato soup which did not pair well with any of the items that were ordered. I also asked for ranch sauce as well which they forgot to add to my order when I left - that would have been the saving grace to those tenders.

With a plethora of sauce that this place has to offer, I'm sure that I would have a better experience with a different flavor profile. But will I be back? I'm not too sure. I do like how they offer other items on their menu such as sandwiches and wraps. Might visit another location within the Houston area. I was just left unimpressed. Thankfully the meal wasn't as salty or aggressively fried in flavor as other fast foods spots. Slim' ranking for this spot. But might revisit if having a hankering for some tenders. Unless I'm cravin' for another kinda sauce. Until next time.
PS - they are serving up cheesecake desserts & various pudding jar desserts... perhaps something sweeter and cooling in this heat would be nice.”

blocks.v: Slowpokes’ Upper Kirby outpost brings the brand’s signature laid-back charm right across from Levy Park. With whimsical animal art, a relaxed aesthetic, and plenty of seating, it’s a breezy place to work, socialize, or unwind before a stroll through the park. Three hours of validated garage parking makes it even more appealing for inner-loopers looking to avoid the usual parking chaos.

The café offers a wide range of drinks—coffee, wine, tea, and house snacks—and while the beans run on the stronger, sharper side, the environment makes lingering here easy. Service is friendly, seating is ample, and both indoor and outdoor options keep the space lively but never overwhelming.

“Digging this second location of Slowpokes and liking how it's nestled within the inner loop. The location is stellar—right across Levy park with plenty of parking situated within the garage. You get in a good three hours of free parking within the garage, as long as you get your ticket validated upon leaving the cafe. There's also a bit of outside parking as well within a three hour timeframe.

Upon entering, you'll notice a few whimsical paintings of sloths, snails and turtles. All things cute and slow. Liking the unique concept as well as the decor. Slowpokes has quite a few items in terms of their beverage menu. Plenty of snacks and foodish items as well.

I opted for a latte and asked which sort of syrups they had. The barista recommended a rose latte and that caught my attention rather quickly. Being a fan of rose flavored anything, I went ahead and ordered the latte that she suggested. Service was friendly and the latte was brought promptly to my table. Although I enjoyed my latte, I really couldn't taste any of the rose flavor. The coffee beans are sour and strong here— not the smooth finish type. Latte was generously filled to the brim and I couldn't finish it all.

Next time I'll opt for a cappuccino. Overall I'm diggin' the vibes, music and aesthetic appeal. Nothing hipster, cramped or stuffy about Slowpokes. It's great to have yet another coffee house within Houston—one that I'll definitely frequent.”

blocks.v: This lively Smashburger gathering in the Galleria brought together great weather, good company, and nostalgic comfort food—all the makings of a fun, relaxed mid-April outing. With clear skies overhead, it was the perfect day for burgers, fries, milkshakes, and conversation.

Smashburger has long dotted Houston’s food scene, but this event offered a great excuse to revisit the familiar chain in a social setting. While many attendees opted for burgers, the grilled chicken sandwich held its own—hot, fresh, and served on toasted buns with crisp tomato slices. Though the avocado add-on fell flat (prepackaged in flavor and initially forgotten), the rest of the meal delivered warm satisfaction. The rosemary-dusted tater tots were a standout: crispy, aromatic, and wonderfully seasoned. And the strawberry milkshake? Pure childhood nostalgia in a cup—creamy, sweet, and perfectly paired with a savory plate.
Surrounded by friendly faces and sunny weather, the meetup was a delightful reminder of how simple comfort foods can bring people together.
Grilled chicken sandwich (simple, fresh & toasted buns)

“What a wonderful foodtastic event! Clear and sunny skies called for a milkshake paired with burgers and fries. Smashburger has been around for some time... scattered throughout Houston, but I had barely visited in the past. Simply because I don't eat burgers that often. But are they tasty? Most definitely. Whether stacked, smashed or simply a classic patty no cheese, you can't go wrong.

I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich. Paired it with tator tots and a strawberry milkshake. No frills, just simple. Asked for avocado with my sandwich as well. Meal came out piping hot and fresh. The grilled chicken breast was on the smaller side, but still good. Buns were toasted and the tomato slices were fresh in the sandwich. The only thing that was missing was the avocado — they forgot to put it in the meal so I had to go and grab it. Avocado was a let down because it tasted dull and prepackaged, just as similar as the ones from Sam's club.

Other than that, my meal was good. Fresh rosemary tossed into crispy and warm tator tots? Goood stuff! As well as the sweet and creamy strawberry milkshake paired with the meal. Very nostalgic of childhood.

Met with others as we chowed down on good grub. Twas warm and friendly company on that bright day. Will I revisit this particular Smashburger location? Most definitely. It's central within most spots in the inner loop.

blocks.v: Sugar Land Memorial Park offers a peaceful retreat tucked just far enough from the bustle of daily life. With still, glasslike water winding through its landscape and wide open spaces ideal for walking, fishing, or simply breathing deeply, this park is a serene gem within the suburbs. Winter and spring highlight its beauty even more—cool air, soft sunlight, and the quiet hum of nature set the mood for rest or reflection.

Whether you're bringing friends, family, or furry companions, the spacious grounds and minimal traffic noise make it easy to unwind. The park features a large pavilion near the entrance for gatherings, scenic paths stretching into grassy fields, and occasional closed-off areas near the memorial obelisk. Despite that, there’s plenty of room to roam, move, and reconnect with nature.
What to Enjoy at Sugar Land Memorial Park
Tranquil water views perfect for fishing or quiet contemplation
Long concrete walking paths ideal for exercise
Unique trees and local bird sightings
Peaceful, low-noise environment for strolling or relaxing

“Calm. Clean. Crystal clear. I'm describing this park and the water that stretches throughout the land it's situated on. Very peaceful. You can go fishing near the water or just reflect upon life. I hope you do enough reflections and meditation—maybe this park will inspire you to do just that.

I love visiting this quiet and tucked-away park in the winter and spring seasons. Bring your friends, doggie pals, and family. You don't hear too much traffic noise, especially as you wander far off into the grass. There are a few unique trees and birds here as well.

At the front of the entrance you'll find a cosy yet large pavilion for gatherings and picnics. There's a small section of the park closed for now (near the memorial obelisk). Other than that, there's plenty of concrete to stretch your legs and walk upon. Keep moving. That's always the goal. You'll find that here.”

ld.headline: Sunday Press – A Colorful, Flavor-Packed Café in Garden Oaks
ld.description: Sunday Press is a vibrant, joyful café that feels like a burst of color from the moment you walk in. With an extensive menu, beautiful pastry displays, and a warm neighborhood buzz, this Garden Oaks staple delivers a little something for everyone—whether you're craving a latte, a comfort-filled breakfast taco, or a sweet afternoon treat. Sunday Press fills up quickly, especially in the mornings, but the variety of seating and the energy inside make it a welcoming spot for conversations, studying

blocks.v: Sunday Press is a vibrant, joyful café that feels like a burst of color from the moment you walk in. With an extensive menu, beautiful pastry displays, and a warm neighborhood buzz, this Garden Oaks staple delivers a little something for everyone—whether you're craving a latte, a comfort-filled breakfast taco, or a sweet afternoon treat. Sunday Press fills up quickly, especially in the mornings, but the variety of seating and the energy inside make it a welcoming spot for conversations, studying, remote work, or slow weekend lounging.

The pastry case alone is enough to spark childhood nostalgia and adult-level excitement: marble pound cake, macadamia nut cookies, snickerdoodles, and the rare, highly coveted swirl croissants. The matcha swirl croissant in particular stands out—crispy, flaky, and filled with a balanced earthy sweetness. Drinks are equally satisfying, with the London fog latte offering depth, sweetness, and the subtle kiss of bergamot on creamy foam.
Cookies, pound cakes & pastries behind the glass
Acai bowls, soups, salads, and sandwiches

“My gosh — the menu here is so colorful, fun and quite extensive. You will find something for everyone here! Rejoice. This colorful café in more ways than one is serving up colorful, sweet and intricate food items.

Upon first glance — it's their sweets and treats that keep me coming back for more. Been awhile since I glanced at a marble pound cake, macadamia nut cookie, snickerdoodle and swirly croissants all tucked behind a lovely glass display. Sunday Press has these one of a kind swirl croissants which are hard to find within the city of Houston. This spot serves up these rare gems and on top of that? They're quite good. Great YUM and CRISP factor with the right amount of filling of your choice — my fav being the matcha swirl croissant.

For drinks selections: they've got everything you need! From café lattes, tea lattes and many other beverages to choose from — ours being the london fog latte. Sweet. Depth. And just the right amount of bergamot essence kissing the milky foam of the cup.

In regards to food, you'll find sandwiches, soups, salad among many other items. It's almost hard to decide — I was torn between pasta salad or breakfast taco. I went for the brekkie taco and glad I did. It was one taco yet it was filling, warm and with plenty of flavor. I liked how the taco wasn't spicy and that the tortilla was warm, stretchy and fresh. They added plenty of shredded veggies to my veggie breakfast taco. It was filling and made for the perfect meal earlier in the day. If I'm ever here later in the day, I'll definitely opt for some type of salad to go with my tea.

This spot fills up quick! We got here earlier in the morning and witnessed seats disappearing fast. Thankfully they have plenty of seating of all types. Many folks connecting and chatting while others studying or working on their laptops. With decently warm service within a unique colorful environment — I can definitely see why this place slowly causes traffic jams and gets packed within the day.

I envision myself revisiting again sometime soon and ordering a few different items on the menu. Will be back when in the area, which is once in awhile. Thank you Sunday Press for your treats and good vibes.”
Category: Coffee & Tea, Acai Bowls, Sandwiches
Location: Oak Forest / Garden Oaks, Houston
Tags: Sunday Press Houston, Garden Oaks cafés, swirl croissants Houston, best London fog latte Houston, colorful cafés Texas, breakfast tacos Houston

This tiny, bustling taquería brings big, bright flavors to the table—fresh salsas, warm tortillas, and lovingly prepared plates that echo the warmth of a family kitchen. Grande Avocado Quesadilla – warm, cheesy, generously filled, deeply satisfying
Crispy Tostada – crunchy, flavorful, great with any of the fresh salsas
Tacos (any variety) – vibrant, authentic flavors reminiscent of Yucatán cooking
Aguas Frescas – house-made with real fruit chunks and natural sweetness
Vegetarian Options – beans and tortillas made without lard; try the nopal or soups

“Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole-in-the-wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the Yucatán peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table, but it’s worth it. Tons of to-go orders and tables scattered around the spot, yet the staff are big on courtesy and cleanliness.

There are about six fresh, in-house-made salsas to enjoy, and the aguas frescas are made with real fruit and pulp—sweet, cold, and perfect with savory food. I truly recommend the grande avocado quesadilla and the crispy tostada. Heck, the tacos are great too.

The menu is flexible and accommodating for any palate. Plenty of vegetarian items, and the beans and tortillas are vegetarian (no lard). Bonus points! Looking forward to revisiting and trying the nopal and soup. Glad to have a warm spot like Doña Lena in the neighborhood.”

blocks.v: Taizzi Sushi brings a warm, unpretentious charm to the Katy dining scene. Located in a small, busy plaza near the mall, this compact restaurant offers an unexpectedly varied menu—from sushi to Korean ramen, bibimbap, and poke bowls. Guests can choose between à la carte dining or their popular AYCE option, making it a flexible pick for anything from a quick meal to a leisurely sushi night.

Despite its tight interior, Taizzi delivers impressively attentive service, fast pacing, and a relaxed, dimly lit atmosphere that suits casual dinners. If you enjoy baked sushi, spice-forward rolls, or comforting fusion dishes, this is a welcoming spot to roll with the tides.
Baked Salmon Sushi – tender, warm, and richly flavored
Baked Lobster Sushi – next on the list for baked-sushi lovers
Peppered Tuna Sashimi – bold with a satisfying kick
Pink Lady Roll – flavorful, balanced, and eye-catching
Korean Ramen & Bibimbap – hearty options beyond sushi

“Roll with the tides! Taizzi Sushi in Katy isn't too far from the local mall. Decided to stop by on a whim with a good friend for dinner. I thought the food here was pretty decent. They've got quite a large selection of grub to choose from the menu. I spotted Korean style ramen, bibimbap, and even poke bowls on the menu. This spot is known for their AYCE selection or just wing it a la carte.

Settled in for sushi because that's what this place is known for. First of all, the plaza is tiny and the restaurant is cramped as well. Surprisingly though on a Saturday night, we found decent parking and it wasn't too busy inside—most likely due to the holidays.
Service was impeccable. Since it’s a small space, the servers continuously checked up on us. One of them even offered me a fork since I'm not the biggest fan of using chopsticks. Lol.

My favorite item was the baked sushi. I've always been a fan of baked sushi and they've got a decent selection. The baked salmon sushi we ordered was tender and flavorful. Definitely want to try the baked lobster option next time. Runner up was the peppered tuna sashimi and the Pink Lady sushi—both had a bite and a kick to them.

The jasmine tea wasn't that good though; flat and lukewarm. The interior is dark and cozy, good for a dinner vibe. They've got a TV inside blasting Korean music to keep you awake with all the glutinous rice intake. Taizzi Sushi – Cozy Bites & AYCE Comfort in Katy

Sara LorenFeb 12 min read

Taizzi Sushi brings a warm, unpretentious charm to the Katy dining scene. Located in a small, busy plaza near the mall, this compact restaurant offers an unexpectedly varied menu—from sushi to Korean ramen, bibimbap, and poke bowls. Guests can choose between à la carte dining or their popular AYCE option, making it a flexible pick for anything from a quick meal to a leisurely sushi night.


Despite its tight interior, Taizzi delivers impressively attentive service, fast pacing, and a relaxed, dimly lit atmosphere that suits casual dinners. If you enjoy baked sushi, spice-forward rolls, or comforting fusion dishes, this is a welcoming spot to roll with the tides.


Must-Try Items:

  • Baked Salmon Sushi – tender, warm, and richly flavored

  • Baked Lobster Sushi – next on the list for baked-sushi lovers

  • Peppered Tuna Sashimi – bold with a satisfying kick

  • Pink Lady Roll – flavorful, balanced, and eye-catching

  • Korean Ramen & Bibimbap – hearty options beyond sushi


Reviews

Sara I. (Apr 17, 2022): 

“Roll with the tides! Taizzi Sushi in Katy isn't too far from the local mall. Decided to stop by on a whim with a good friend for dinner. I thought the food here was pretty decent. They've got quite a large selection of grub to choose from the menu. I spotted Korean style ramen, bibimbap, and even poke bowls on the menu. This spot is known for their AYCE selection or just wing it a la carte.


Settled in for sushi because that's what this place is known for. First of all, the plaza is tiny and the restaurant is cramped as well. Surprisingly though on a Saturday night, we found decent parking and it wasn't too busy inside—most likely due to the holidays.


Service was impeccable. Since it’s a small space, the servers continuously checked up on us. One of them even offered me a fork since I'm not the biggest fan of using chopsticks. Lol.


My favorite item was the baked sushi. I've always been a fan of baked sushi and they've got a decent selection. The baked salmon sushi we ordered was tender and flavorful. Definitely want to try the baked lobster option next time. Runner up was the peppered tuna sashimi and the Pink Lady sushi—both had a bite and a kick to them.


The jasmine tea wasn't that good though; flat and lukewarm. The interior is dark and cozy, good for a dinner vibe. They've got a TV inside blasting Korean music to keep you awake with all the glutinous rice intake. Wouldn’t mind revisiting when around the area—especially after shopping and settling in for cozy starch bombs. That's what sushi is after all, am I right? Lol. Keep it local & prosper! blocks.v: Teapresso Bar in Sugar Land brings a Hawaiian-inspired twist to the local café scene, offering Kona coffee, milk teas, hot beverages, and customizable drinks with organic coffee beans—something not easily found in this part of town. With warm wooden tables, bright interiors, and plenty of seating, it’s a convenient place to study, work, or wind down with a drink.

However, the experience can be hit-or-miss. Once known for friendly service and quality drinks, this location has seen a noticeable decline in customer care, atmosphere, and consistency. Prices have crept up, and the staff’s demeanor has grown increasingly aloof. Still, for locals seeking real milk (not powdered creamer) and solid coffee options, Teapresso Bar remains one of the few alternatives in Sugar Land.

The café continues to shine in its cleanliness, available seating, and steady drink lineup. But with a little more warmth and attentiveness, it could easily return to its former charm—especially in a city craving more unique coffee and tea destinations.
Can get loud during drink preparation

“This spot was unusually warm today and the service was mediocre at best; which seems to be the case lately. I've always liked Teapresso and really dig the location out in the Heights.. (if it's still around). But this location in the heart of Sugar Land could do way better. They were great when they first started out.. which was about 4 years ago. Since then the service has gone downhill and the drinks are steep in price.

The young lady at the front never smiles and seems to be irritated at any cost. Nonetheless, some of the drinks are still okay and it's one of the few spots where you can actually get a decent cup of coffee in Sugar Land. Simply because you have an option for choosing organic coffee beans and actual milk in your drinks. I always steer clear from non-dairy creamer and crap coffee.

I appreciate the fact that we have a Hawaiian style cafe in town that specializes in tapioca drinks, Kona coffee and a few other items. They have snacks as well as a few hot beverages. Plenty of seating with warm wooden tables and board games as well. It's a decent spot to get some work done or work on anything on your laptop. It can get loud at times because they're obviously making drinks in the corner.

All in all, it's a good spot in the area, especially with limited coffee choices (c'mon Sugar Land!). A bit bleak at times.. hoping they can regain their charm. Plus side? Always clean and bright inside.”
Tags: Teapresso Bar Sugar Land review, Kona coffee Houston suburbs, bubble tea Sugar Land, Hawaiian-style café Texas, organic coffee Sugar Land, study cafés Houston area

blocks.v: Terry Hershey Park is one of Houston’s most beloved green escapes—an expansive, tree-lined sanctuary tucked right into the bustle of the Energy Corridor. With multiple entrances that each lead to different winding paths, bridges, and leafy tunnels, the park feels both vast and intimate, offering something for walkers, runners, bicyclists, and nature lovers alike.

Its long corridors of trees create shaded pathways that stretch for miles, making it easy to get wonderfully lost in the scenery. Hidden pockets of charm appear throughout the park, from neighborhood-adjacent corners to community-decorated benches and even a tiny outdoor library where visitors can borrow or leave a book. Seasonal beauty shines here—especially in spring and autumn, when wildflowers glow and cooler air turns afternoon walks into something magical.
Whether you're seeking movement, fresh air, or a peaceful reset, Terry Hershey Park remains a treasured reminder of nature’s resilience within Houston’s “concrete jungle.”
Bridges connecting different sections of the park
Hidden neighborhood corners with charming touches (like a mini library!)
Seasonal scenery—especially spring wildflowers and autumn strolls

Sara I. (May 25, 2022): “A rather large yet cozy park smacked in the middle of the energy corridor. There are various entrances to reach this park; & yet each entrance happens to guide you through a unique path. I love the large stretched out corridors here. These are tunnels that are full of trees that stretch so far out into various pathways and bridges. Great for those that are joggers or bicyclists. I find myself mostly walking here and yet I can't seem to finish the trail. It's easy to get lost here as well. Lol. Unless you spot a map or something.

As mentioned, the trails are long and unwinding. I had always known about this park yet its entrances were mysterious, and easily missed. Frequently visiting and being near the beltway, I was able to spot one of the main entrances and that was it. I've been a frequent stroller here for the past 2 years.

This park seems to have been here forever; I hope it stays & that it continues to preserve itself within the midst of the concrete jungle. There are vast neighborhoods tucked within the corners of some of the pathways. One of the neighbors decorated a bench and left a mini library outside so walkers can grab books & leave a book as well. It's these little things that are precious & that have made this park ever so charming.

I love visiting in Autumn and Spring in particular. Last year I spotted a field of yellow flowers. Just nothing but pure yellow gold all around, as if the sun had dipped its beams into the earth. Support local parks, walk, bike or jog. Or bring your fluffy best friend. Just move a bit and you'll be good! Toodles!”
Tags: Terry Hershey Park review, Energy Corridor parks, Houston hiking trails, nature walks Houston, best jogging trails Houston, scenic parks Houston

“This restaurant really brought in the heat. I thought I could handle any spice level until I met Thai Orchid on a random Sunday night. The best items on the menu are definitely the Laotian and Cambodian-influenced dishes. The Som Tum is the total winner—super crisp, sour, and spicy. I honestly couldn’t handle the heat at first, but after a moment to catch my breath, I inhaled most of it. The Thai iced coffee was the saving grace.

The Tom Yum had plenty of depth and zest, packed with fresh tomatoes, shrimp, and mushrooms, and can be made vegetarian. I loved their Laad Nah—dark gravy, broccoli, onions, and chicken, savory and slightly sweet, and a great balance to the spicy dishes.

The menu is huge, the food is fresh, and the owners are friendly. Decor is simple, but the flavors shine. If you’re in North Houston or passing through Spring, I recommend stopping by. Support local biz!”

blocks.v: The Grove Donutz & Deli offers a mix of nostalgic, simple donuts alongside their well-known extravagant “monster” creations. Tucked away in the quieter stretches of Richmond, this shop has become a go-to for those craving soft yeast donuts, classic glazes, and a few fun, whimsical options. While their social media shows off their over-the-top creations, the real charm lies in their traditional offerings—soft, stretchy dough, balanced sweetness, and comfort in every bite.
Excellent classic donuts: cinnamon twists, cinnamon buns, and the playful “Homer” pink glazed donut
Fresh, hot coffee with strong flavor
A menu that extends into savory territory: kolaches, tacos, and sandwiches
Custom donuts vary in consistency—better for adventurous eaters than purists

“I’m normally not a fan of monster-like donuts—the custom ones loaded with crazy ingredients. Fun to look at, creative even, but taste-wise? Meh. I’m a simple donut gal. Give me a chocolate-glazed, a sprinkle donut, or a soft cinnamon twist and I’m happy.

The cinnamon twists here are my absolute favorite—soft, stretchy, yeast-like, and just lightly glazed. The Homer donut with pink frosting and sprinkles is another sweet treat; the subtle strawberry flavor is cute and nostalgic. The custom French toast donut, though? Hit or miss. My recent trip was a total miss. The whipped cream melted instantly, and the whole thing tasted overwhelmingly of batter—soggy and unimpressive. Their Instagram photos look incredible, so it’s disappointing when the real thing doesn’t match.

On a brighter note, the lemon jelly donut was yummy, and the coffee was fresh, hot, and strong. They offer savory items like fusion tacos, sandwiches, kolaches, and croissants—honestly, I think their savory creativity fares better than their sweet experiments.
This spot is still a fun little pick-me-up in the middle of sleepy Richmond. A great place for a classic donut and coffee. Support local, enjoy something simple, and wash those hands. ;)”

Sara I. (Apr 3, 2020): 

“I’m normally not a fan of monster-like donuts—the custom ones loaded with crazy ingredients. Fun to look at, creative even, but taste-wise? Meh. I’m a simple donut gal. Give me a chocolate-glazed, a sprinkle donut, or a soft cinnamon twist and I’m happy.


The cinnamon twists here are my absolute favorite—soft, stretchy, yeast-like, and just lightly glazed. The Homer donut with pink frosting and sprinkles is another sweet treat; the subtle strawberry flavor is cute and nostalgic. The custom French toast donut, though? Hit or miss. My recent trip was a total miss. The whipped cream melted instantly, and the whole thing tasted overwhelmingly of batter—soggy and unimpressive. Their Instagram photos look incredible, so it’s disappointing when the real thing doesn’t match.


On a brighter note, the lemon jelly donut was yummy, and the coffee was fresh, hot, and strong. They offer savory items like fusion tacos, sandwiches, kolaches, and croissants—honestly, I think their savory creativity fares better than their sweet experiments.


This spot is still a fun little pick-me-up in the middle of sleepy Richmond. A great place for a classic donut and coffee. Support local, enjoy something simple, and wash those hands. ;)”

From there, you’ll park in the garage below, then take the elevator up to the first floor to check in. Simple, clear, and orderly.

One quick heads-up: the café was not open yet at the time of this visit, so if you’re planning a longer stop, consider grabbing a drink or snack beforehand.

blocks.v: The Oceanaire Seafood Room is a long-standing Galleria favorite—known for its sleek, submarine-inspired design, large corner windows overlooking bustling streets, and over two decades of reputation as a premier seafood destination. It’s the kind of restaurant many Houstonians keep on their “must-visit” list. During Houston Restaurant Weeks, expectations run especially high, but this particular visit offered a mix of highs and lows.

While the ambiance and several dishes impressed, service inconsistencies impacted the overall experience. Still, the restaurant’s strengths—fresh sushi, flavorful appetizers, and a stellar key lime pie—hint at its potential when firing on all cylinders. With such an iconic Houston presence, a return visit to explore the regular menu feels worthwhile.
Iconic Galleria location with a submarine-inspired aesthetic
Fresh, flavorful sushi & excellent smoked salmon starter
Tasty shrimp fried rice, though served lukewarm due to service delays
Key lime pie: tart, refreshing, and one of the best
Service during HRW was inattentive and lacked communication
Regular menu appears strong—worth revisiting outside HRW
“3 stars experience during Houston Restaurant Weeks. Boy, were we all excited to dine in at this restaurant. It is a Houston classic!

From the submarine looking terrain, to the large windows at the corner facing one of the busiest streets in Houston. It's the Galleria after all, and it’s one of the most popular spots to visit. This restaurant has been around for over 20 years, and for some of us, it was our very first time.

I do believe they could have had better choices in regards to their food menu with HRW. This is all in regards to food allergies, mind you. So that’s something we take seriously. But we came on a mission! To dine in on HRW style menu which benefits the local Houston Food Bank.

Their regular menu looks great and appealing. We may revisit and try items from their everyday menu. We did try their sushi and we loved it. The sushi was fresh and flavorful. It retained its shape well and came with a burst of flavor. My second favorite was the smoked salmon. It was chunky, held its shape and it had a great umami yet mellow flavor as well. Paired well with the bold marinated onions, capers, relish and crispy crackers.

I did like the shrimp fried rice, it was flavorful and well seasoned — however it was quite lukewarm by the time it reached our table. Reason being? They forgot to deliver our order to the table. We waited for ages after being served appetizers. So much time passed by that I had to flag down a waiter from far away, just to get his notice and ask him what happened to our food?

He quickly went in, back of the house and grabbed our meals. So basically our meals were sitting BOH, chillin and getting cold. No apologies or ‘I'm sorry for the delay in your food.’ Instead he mentioned, ‘Oh, we're packed and having a busy day here.’ Definitely didn't seem like it, with most of the room being empty. Just one day before, my entire office dined in here for HRW. What must have happened then? Not enough employees to accommodate diners needs. Lack of customer service was the downfall of our experience dining here at the Oceanaire.

Dessert was good. It was ordered from their regular menu as it’s not provided with HRW. We opted for the key lime pie and it was definitely one of the better ones we've all had. Super tart, sweet and refreshing. Perfect on the palate after consuming mellow oceanic foods.

Again, we all enjoyed our food. Totally look forward to revisiting and trying items from their regular menu. This is a nice spot to bring out-of-town guests. They have many non-seafood items as well for those that aren't much into seafood. We're just hoping for warmer and keen attentive service next time around for such a posh and elaborate spot such as this. Until next time!”

ld.description: A long-loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old-world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada. blocks.v: A long-loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old-world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada. The interior glows with nostalgic character, and the atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming—plus, the owners’ friendly cats occasionally roam outside, adding even more personality to this neighborhood gem. With an extensive menu spanning savory classics, creative fillings, and sweet dessert blends, there’s truly an empanada for everyone.
Beef Picadillo (Beef Gaucho) – Juicy, classic, and the perfect pairing with green chili sauce.
Chicken Poblana (Mole) – Earthy, deep chocolate notes, rich and comforting.
Dessert Empanada: Elvis Melbis – Peanut butter + banana + dulce de leche indulgence.

“They have cats upon the premises! That's the main reason I dined in here a couple of days ago. Jk. I had dinner here a few nights ago with a good friend. Both of the cats belong to the owners and normally just patrol outside—not inside.

This was my first time at Marini's, though my friend Mike had been here before. The interior is warm and glowing, with plenty of seating. There’s a historical appeal inside Marini’s, and I'm surprised it took me so long to visit.

On a crisp and chilly night, empanadas were just the right items to nosh on. The menu is large and thoroughly categorized—there’s truly an empanada for everyone. I ordered two savory empanadas and one dessert: the chicken poblana (mole), the beef picadillo (beef gaucho), and the Elvis melbis for dessert (peanut butter, banana, dulce de leche).

Everything is made fresh to order, and the taste reflects the quality. Service was prompt and attentive. All three empanadas were delicious—warm, crispy, freshly fried. I couldn’t finish them all and took a few bites to-go. The chicken mole was deep, earthy, and had a unique savory chocolate flavor. My favorite was the beef picadillo—juicy and perfect with the green chili sauce. When it comes to empanadas, I prefer fried over baked, and these were executed beautifully.

The dessert empanada was rich and sweet—the dulce de leche paired nicely with the banana and peanut butter, though I’ll try another flavor next time. With so many options, I look forward to exploring more of the menu. Marini’s also serves soups, salads, and more. Since it carries an Argentinian flair, you’ll find iced yerba mate by the counter. It was watered down in flavor, but still refreshing.
Chill atmosphere and warm food for the soul. Try the Original Marini’s for yourself—it's a Houston classic.
PS – I might just revisit to hang out with the cats.”

blocks.v: Tucked beneath a canopy of trees along Grogan’s Drive, Third Gen Coffee feels like a cozy escape—a quiet, woodsy nook with nostalgic winter charm and the warmth of a true neighborhood café. From the moment you step inside, its character shines through: soft lighting, inviting décor, and the unexpected charm of a staircase that leads to a peaceful second-floor lounge.

Upstairs, guests find couches, tables, and charging outlets, making it an ideal setting for studying, reading, or lingering with a warm drink. Seasonal beverages bring extra joy, and the standout this visit was a hot eggnog latte—creamy, festive, and deliciously comforting.

Friendly service and thoughtfully crafted drinks round out the experience, making Third Gen Coffee a must-visit for those seeking a serene moment in The Woodlands. Whether you’re passing through or planning a cozy café day, this corner shop offers warmth, charm, and the kind of atmosphere that invites you to return again and again.

“Such a great little coffee shoppe tucked in the Woodlands on Grograns drive. I'm diggin' this quiet little corner, cluttered with trees and a few stores lined up together. The air felt & smelled crisp and it totally was nostalgic of some sort of northern winter. Wanting to visit the local bookshop next time.

What I liked most about this coffee shoppe? It's charm and characteristic. That's the first thing I noticed upon stepping in. A bit of light and warmth all around, and a staircase that leads you to the second floor. Ample seating upstairs with a few tables, couch and charging outlets.

They have a few unique flavoured drinks this time of the year. My favorite being the eggnog latte.. but make it hot. I look forward to revisiting and trying different items off the menu, in particular, their seasonal products.
It was a great local experience at third gen coffee, the staff was friendly and the drinks were crafted with love. I totally look forward to revisiting if ever in the area.”

blocks.v: Tim Hortons may be a Canadian legend, but its charming Katy outpost feels right at home in the Texas suburbs. Tucked into a quiet corner of town, this cozy café offers a nostalgic, no-fuss approach to coffee and baked treats—a welcome change from trend-heavy cafés.

Famous across Canada for its reliable drip coffee, donuts, Timbits, and breakfast staples, Tim Hortons brings a touch of northern comfort to Katy. The hot coffee here is simple and satisfying, especially when paired with a tender cake donut dusted lightly with nutmeg—perfect for dunking. While some of the other donuts leaned a bit dry, the holiday flavors and assortment of baked goods still add to the fun.

The menu also features savory options, including avocado toast, which was just okay but offered balance among all the sweets. With festive seasonal beverages and classic cold brews available, there’s something for every type of coffee drinker.

The café’s interior is small but warm and inviting, infused with Canadian-themed décor that adds to its charm. Service is decent, though the drive-thru can get chaotic—making the dine-in experience the better choice.

Tim Hortons in Katy is a sweet little gem for a cozy winter morning, a donut-and-coffee break, or a quick suburban caffeine fix. And with more locations on the horizon, Texans may soon enjoy even more of Canada’s favorite grab-and-go coffee spot.
Cake donut (nutmeg-kissed, tender, perfect for dunking)
Cold brew vanilla (if you’re in the mood for something chilled)
“Such a great little gem of a coffee shoppe tucked in a quiet corner within the suburbs of Katy, TX.

Tim Horton's is originally from Canada.. & is all the rage up in the northern hemisphere... & I can totally see why! It is considered Canada's favorite coffee on the run. This spot specializes in both hot and cold coffee drinks, as well as donuts, pastries and a few savory items.
Had heard about Tim Hortons back in the day.. just hadn't ventured out to Canada in awhile. I am glad we have a location here in TX, which is soon to spread out within neighboring cities.

Hot coffee was great.. nice and simple. Drip coffee paired with a donut? Keeping it old school. I didn't care for any cold bevvie that day.. but my friend's cold brew vanilla drink looked good. Plenty of holiday flavors this time of the year as well.

They have a variety of donuts to choose from.. my favorite being the cake donut. Tender and sprinkled a bit with nutmeg. Dunk it into hot coffee.. bliss. The other donuts were on the drier side & didn't taste fresh. That's too bad because this spot specializes in their sweet treats. Also tried their avocado toast which was just okay. I'm glad they have a bit of savory items to balance with all the sweetness.

Interior is quite small.. but cozy. Decor is quite heartwarming and very Canadian. Service was okay.. could be better. Their drive thru seemed chaotic and I totally recommend visiting the interior of the cafe.

All in all, a great spot to set up shoppe. I'll definitely revisit in the near future. Here's hoping we can get more Hortons on the way.. because ‘Horton hears a who! & A why not?!’ Lol. Totally a Dr Seuss reference.. if you know, you know. Cheers and happy coffee drinking during the coziest month of the year!”

blocks.v: Tønsberg Brygge sits at the heart of Norway’s oldest town—a place steeped in Viking history, maritime heritage, and quiet Scandinavian charm. The waterfront is a picturesque blend of cobblestone streets, historic boats, crisp coastal air, and cafés that line the serene pier. Whether you’re exploring the town’s deep cultural roots or simply wandering along the water, the brygge captures the tranquil, introspective beauty of Norwegian life.

The town itself is layered with history: Viking origins from the 9th century, important trading routes, and solemn stories preserved in its old cemetery, which holds war graves from the Battle of Jutland. Yet despite its historical weight, Tønsberg feels light and peaceful—a place where the days move slowly, the water mirrors the sky, and reflection feels natural.
What to Experience at Tønsberg Brygge
Tranquil waterfront views along the pier
Cobblestone streets near the shopping district
Seasonal farmers markets with fresh, local seafood
Historical boat launches during the holiday season
Cafés and restaurants lining the water
A quiet, small-town atmosphere perfect for reflection

“Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town—historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. Founded by Vikings in the 9th century, it later became an important trading center. Tonsberg Old Cemetery even contains 22 war graves from the First World War, 14 of them unidentified, all naval casualties from the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

The town is charming with its cobblestone streets, especially near the shopping district. I lived here back in 2017 for about half a year, and visiting the brygge (pier) was always a tranquil escape. Many restaurants line the pier, some offering diverse cuisine. Food in Norway wasn’t my favorite overall, but there was a decent Indian restaurant by the water. Local seafood was fresh and often displayed at the farmers market.

The pier would be freezing in autumn and winter. During the holiday season, townsfolk launch their old historical boats—an incredible sight. Many cafés and restaurants close early, and grocery stores were closed on Sundays, which was a bit of a culture shock as an American. Yet these differences brought introspection and deep personal growth. The icy, glasslike water felt like a mirror for self-reflection.
I may have been on the outside looking in, but it was a beautiful, ponderous ride. I recommend visiting the pier and experiencing this quiet, elegant town.”

The town itself is layered with history: Viking origins from the 9th century, important trading routes, and solemn stories preserved in its old cemetery, which holds war graves from the Battle of Jutland. Yet despite its historical weight, Tønsberg feels light and peaceful—a place where the days move slowly, the water mirrors the sky, and reflection feels natural.


What to Experience at Tønsberg Brygge

  • Tranquil waterfront views along the pier

  • Cobblestone streets near the shopping district

  • Seasonal farmers markets with fresh, local seafood

  • Historical boat launches during the holiday season

  • Cafés and restaurants lining the water

  • A quiet, small-town atmosphere perfect for reflection


Review

Sara I. (Feb 10, 2022): 

“Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town—historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. Founded by Vikings in the 9th century, it later became an important trading center. Tonsberg Old Cemetery even contains 22 war graves from the First World War, 14 of them unidentified, all naval casualties from the Battle of Jutland in 1916.


The town is charming with its cobblestone streets, especially near the shopping district. I lived here back in 2017 for about half a year, and visiting the brygge (pier) was always a tranquil escape. Many restaurants line the pier, some offering diverse cuisine. Food in Norway wasn’t my favorite overall, but there was a decent Indian restaurant by the water. Local seafood was fresh and often displayed at the farmers market.


The pier would be freezing in autumn and winter. During the holiday season, townsfolk launch their old historical boats—an incredible sight. Many cafés and restaurants close early, and grocery stores were closed on Sundays, which was a bit of a culture shock as an American. Yet these differences brought introspection and deep personal growth. The icy, glasslike water felt like a mirror for self-reflection.


I may have been on the outside looking in, but it was a beautiful, ponderous ride. I recommend visiting the pier and experiencing this quiet, elegant town.”

blocks.v: Verbena Coffee is a warm, wood-toned retreat tucked into the Memorial/Energy Corridor area—a neighborhood café that has quickly grown into a beloved local staple. With Scandinavian-inspired interiors, thoughtfully crafted drinks, and collaborations with nearby bakeries and pop-ups, it’s the kind of space that invites you to slow down on a rainy morning or tuck in for a cozy afternoon recharge.

The drink menu leans comforting and aromatic, featuring house-made syrups, quality loose-leaf teas, and espresso beverages that highlight balance over excess sweetness. Whether you're a coffee devotee or a tea enthusiast, Verbena offers something crafted with intention.
London Fog Latte – loose-leaf Earl Grey steeped in foamy milk with fragrant vanilla
Brown Sugar Latte – lightly sweet, house-made syrup; add cinnamon for extra warmth
Local loaf cakes & croissants – baked goods delivered fresh from nearby partners

“Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn’t even been open for two years. They’re thriving in the Memorial area and it’s wonderful supporting local. I love visiting independently owned coffee shoppes and trying the drinks they craft in house.

My favorite here is the London Fog latte—close to my heart, and not everyone makes it right. Their loose-leaf Earl Grey steeped in warm, foamy milk with fragrant vanilla is perfect. The bergamot is sharp and comforting, especially on a gray and rainy day.

Coffee drinks are just as good. The brown sugar latte, made with their house syrup, isn’t overly sweet—adding cinnamon makes the flavor pop. Cappuccinos are solid too. I’m looking forward to trying their sliced loaf cakes and croissants from a local bakery.
The interior is woodsy and tan, very Scandinavian. They also host pop-ups with other cafés like Koffeteria. Always something fun happening at this neighborhood spot. Until next time.”

blocks.v: Voodoo Doughnut brings its signature pink flair and eccentric personality to Houston—but the experience doesn’t quite match the magic of its flagship locations in Portland or Austin. While the shop is undeniably fun, colorful, and great for hosting out-of-town visitors, the freshness and texture of the doughnuts can be inconsistent compared to their busier, higher-volume counterparts.

Houston is full of standout donut shops, many of which offer simple, fresh, reliable classics. Voodoo leans heavily into novelty toppings and funky combinations—sometimes fun, sometimes too over the top. Yet in the middle of that theatrical menu, the simplest donuts end up being the unexpected stars.
Playful, quirky donut names and bright pink-themed décor
Less foot traffic = less frequent fresh batches
Best items tend to be the classic, uncomplicated donuts
Good hot coffee to pair with your picks

“The doughnuts here aren’t as fresh as the Austin location. They’re not churning through batches the way they do in PDX or ATX, so things get a bit stale. The storefront lacks the charm of the original shops too. Houston has so many great donut spots—and this one just isn’t it for me.

I do enjoy the quirky pink aesthetic and their fun, funky donut names. Definitely a cute place to take visitors. But many toppings are overkill; more hype than substance. The jelly donut was the standout—full of raspberry jelly with a crisp, thick shell. The plain cake donut was another favorite: nutmeg-kissed, dense, not too sweet. The buttermilk bar was good as well. Basically, the simpler the flavor, the better it tasted.
Voodoo is supposed to be magically delicious, but things are getting stale—literally. On the bright side, the coffee is good, warm, local, and fresh. Ask for milk and pair it with your fave donut.
Overall? Probably won’t be back anytime soon.”

It’s the kind of place that keeps evolving, making each visit a little different from the last.

With new shops popping up regularly and colorful, family-friendly stops like TESO Life bringing 90s-inspired fun, WoW is becoming a weekend stroll favorite. Claw machines glow with neon charm, Sanrio characters make surprise appearances, and there’s a sense of joyful exploration woven into the experience. Whether you're running errands, meeting a friend, or simply wandering, this plaza delivers a cheerful dose of nostalgia and discovery.
Vibrant mix of boutiques, cafés, and specialty shops
TESO Life with fun 90s-style claw machines
A still-growing plaza worth revisiting as new vendors move in
“I remember when Mark pointed out WoW plaza back in 2023... it was an empty lot. We were hanging out that day, running on some Trader Joe's errands. Lol.

pages.h1: Windmill Market & Produce – The Iconic Date Shake Stop of North Palm Springs

ld.headline: Windmill Market & Produce – The Iconic Date Shake Stop of North Palm Springs
ld.description: There are road trip treats—and then there are Palm Springs date shakes, the kind that feel like a rite of passage when traveling through the desert. blocks.v: There are road trip treats—and then there are Palm Springs date shakes, the kind that feel like a rite of passage when traveling through the desert. Windmill Market & Produce, nestled among the iconic spinning turbines of North Palm Springs, serves one of the most memorable versions you’ll taste: thick, creamy, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.

Made with fresh locally grown dates, their classic vanilla date shake is rich in flavor with warm caramel notes that taste almost like brown sugar melting into cold cream. The texture is luscious and velvety, and the dates practically dissolve on the tongue. It’s the perfect refreshment after exploring Joshua Tree or cruising through the Yucca Valley.

Beyond shakes, the market sells beautifully packaged fresh dates—ideal for snacking or gifting. The coconut-rolled dates are a standout, offering a sweet, tropical twist. Friendly and efficient service adds to the charm, making it an easy and comforting stop during a desert drive.
Windmill Market is a slice of local flavor infused with a sense of place—surrounded by towering windmills, sunbaked mountains, and all the nostalgic vibes of a classic California road trip.
Vanilla ice cream fresh date shake (the original, the icon)
Other fresh date varieties to take home

“The fresh date shake here was marvelous.. thick in viscosity, creamy and out of this world. The aroma reminded me of brown sugar and the flavor was warm, even though it was a cold and creamy milkshake. They use fresh dates that are commonly grown near and around the palm springs area.

We didn't get to venture too deep within Palm Springs, but this was the closest market to us when we were venturing out of Joshua Tree. Folks were friendly and efficient with their service. We opted for the vanilla ice cream date shake, which is the original flavor here. The dates just melt in your mouth and are totally otherworldly, along with the fresh packaged dates that you can purchase here. They make for a great gift as well, and there are plenty of different flavors — my favorite being the dates rolled in dessicated coconut.
All in all, this is a pretty neat spot. I'd love to revisit and try their savory foods and other items as well.

Geographically, it's super cool to be surrounded by windmills nearby, literally and figuratively. When around and passing through the Yucca Valley, you can count on Windmill Market & Produce for a great beverage and perhaps a snack or two while cruising through your road trip. :) Until next time!”
Category: Grocery, Fruits & Veggies, Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt

blocks.v: World Market in Stafford offers a vibrant, culturally rich escape—perfect for anyone who thrives on global flavors, décor, and eclectic treasures. Though smaller than the long-established Post Oak location, this newer store still brings an impressive spread of international goods, pantry staples, and uniquely crafted home items. From European chocolates to Middle Eastern spices, from artisan mugs to bright textiles, the store feels like a tiny world tour tucked inside the suburbs.

Service is warm, the ambiance is cozy, and the aisles are full of delightful surprises—halal gummy candies, curated teas, candles, cookware, pottery, and seasonal imports that keep each visit fresh. For anyone craving the joy of travel during quiet seasons or limited movement, this shop becomes an unexpected comfort.
Candles, pottery, and unique ceramic bowls

“It is wonderful to explore this culturally diverse store during limited moments of traveling. Anything cultural and world related excites the heck out of me. Thank y’all for opening this store during such obscure times.

World Market has always been a favorite of mine—we had a Sugar Land location over a decade ago, where I’d grab all my culinary staples. It closed long ago, so having one in Stafford now, just minutes from Sugar Land, is such a treat.

This location feels smaller than the Post Oak one, but there’s still so much to browse: candles, spices, halal gummy candies, chocolate (the German marzipan is my favorite!), and a lovely selection of British and international teas. The mugs, bowls, and pottery are beautiful as well.

If you’re into cultural and global goods like I am, you’ll dig this store. It’s my home away from home. Good service and warm ambiance. When the travel bug bites, I make my way to World Market. Until next time. Adeus!”

Yogurtland is a sweet spot to drop by for a cup of yogurt before strolling around the mall. I’ll definitely be back to try new flavors. Until next time!”

blocks.v: Yomie’s Rice X Yogurt brings a unique concept to Chinatown with its lineup of creamy, rice-based and yogurt-based beverages. These drinks are mellow, smooth, and lightly sweet—ideal after a spicy meal or when you’re craving something cooling and indulgent. The menu is playful and creative, though first-time visitors may find the ordering experience a bit unclear. Flavors lean mild and gentle rather than tart or punchy, making this a spot best suited for those who enjoy softer yogurt profiles.
Dragon Fruit Series (when fruit is in season)

“Service was super awkward, cold, and dry—just like the cutting winds outside that night. The drinks were okay: simple yogurt-based beverages that were creamy and mellow. I prefer sharper, tangier yogurt flavors, almost Mediterranean style, and theirs reminded me more of an Australian yogurt—light without any real zest. The dragon fruit didn’t shine through the yogurt at all, maybe because it wasn’t in season.

I did enjoy the yogurt and oats drink, though I wished it had more flavor. It wasn’t too sweet, which I appreciated since I asked for reduced sweetness. I was curious if fruit could be added to the oat drink—definitely a missed opportunity! The menu wasn’t explained to me, adding to the awkwardness.

These cold yogurt drinks are great after a spicy meal; the lactic base totally cuts the acid reflux. I couldn’t finish my drink and refrigerated the rest, thinking it might turn into overnight oats. Nope—the yogurt separated and tasted unpleasant the next day. Oops! Will I return? Maybe. But the service really needs improvement.”

blocks.v: Yummy’s Hot Chicken takes the ever-popular hot chicken trend and elevates it with a bold Syrian twist. This unassuming food truck delivers layers of flavor, crunch, and spice that set it apart from the typical fried-chicken lineup. The menu may be small, but each item is crafted with intention—crispy textures, vibrant toppings, and spice levels that range from gentle heat to full-on fire.

The chicken stays remarkably juicy beneath its golden crust, and the bright slaw adds a refreshing snap that balances the richness. Fans of creative comfort food will appreciate the unique touches, including Middle Eastern-inspired seasoning blends and their standout curry fries. Grab your order early, especially in hot weather—the food is worth savoring before the Houston heat kicks in.
Syrian Hot Chicken Sandwich (medium spice recommended) – crisp, fresh, full of layered flavor
Curry Fries – fragrant curry sauce blended with cheese; hot, bold, and delicious
Chicken Tender Basket – same addictive seasoning in tender form
Challah Bun Option – soft, slightly sweet, and a perfect match for the heat
“Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist.

This sandwich was hecka good—lots of flavor, layers, and textures. Yummy’s has a small, simple menu, but every item overdelivers. I rarely eat anything fried, but their unique twist puts this sandwich in a league of its own. The slaw is bright and vibrant, and the chicken crust is crisp and golden.

They offer different spice levels; I chose medium and it was just right. The curry fries were surprisingly delicious—an interesting fusion with curry sauce meshed into mild cheese sauce, and they arrived steaming hot. My sandwich came on a challah bun instead of a pretzel bun, and I loved it. Definitely ask which bun they’re using.

Everything was crisp and yummy. This spot packs heat and taste. I’ll probably revisit in the fall—eating outside in summer was an adventure in itself! Thanks, Yummy’s. Hope y’all continue to thrive in the Galleria food truck park.”
Category: Food Trucks, Chicken Shop, Sandwiches

The menu may be small, but each item is crafted with intention—crispy textures, vibrant toppings, and spice levels that range from gentle heat to full-on fire.


The chicken stays remarkably juicy beneath its golden crust, and the bright slaw adds a refreshing snap that balances the richness. Fans of creative comfort food will appreciate the unique touches, including Middle Eastern-inspired seasoning blends and their standout curry fries. Grab your order early, especially in hot weather—the food is worth savoring before the Houston heat kicks in.


Must-Try Items

  • Syrian Hot Chicken Sandwich (medium spice recommended) – crisp, fresh, full of layered flavor

  • Curry Fries – fragrant curry sauce blended with cheese; hot, bold, and delicious

  • Chicken Tender Basket – same addictive seasoning in tender form

  • Challah Bun Option – soft, slightly sweet, and a perfect match for the heat


Review

Sara I. (Aug 16, 2020): 

“Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist.

This sandwich was hecka good—lots of flavor, layers, and textures. Yummy’s has a small, simple menu, but every item overdelivers. I rarely eat anything fried, but their unique twist puts this sandwich in a league of its own. The slaw is bright and vibrant, and the chicken crust is crisp and golden.


They offer different spice levels; I chose medium and it was just right. The curry fries were surprisingly delicious—an interesting fusion with curry sauce meshed into mild cheese sauce, and they arrived steaming hot. My sandwich came on a challah bun instead of a pretzel bun, and I loved it. Definitely ask which bun they’re using.

Everything was crisp and yummy. This spot packs heat and taste. I’ll probably revisit in the fall—eating outside in summer was an adventure in itself! Thanks, Yummy’s. Hope y’all continue to thrive in the Galleria food truck park.”

With multiple locations around the city, it’s become a convenient go-to for lunch or dinner. However, experiences can vary—and this visit to the Bellaire location offered a noticeably different impression from others.

While the flavors remained solid—warm spices, tender meats, and enjoyable toppings—the portions at this location felt surprisingly skimpy for the price. The compact, grab-and-go setup and tight parking added to the sense that the visit didn’t quite measure up to the consistency of other Zoa kitchens. For two bowls, one bread, and a green tea totaling around $30, the value simply didn't match the experience, leaving diners still hungry and unsatisfied.
Portions at this location run small for the price

Limited parking & small interior leaning toward takeout

“This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner.

So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their portions and the price point is heavy. For two bowls, 1 bread and 1 green tea, you'll shell out about $30 and leave feeling a bit underwhelmed. Not sure why they are so skimpy with their portions and their service. Food was good, warm and flavorful, but I've had better at their other locations.

This location is quite small and grab and go style as well. Parking is a bit small and limited and as mentioned, this location is smaller than the other ones that I have visited. With the food: The meats were tender and their toppings were decent. Unfortunately, I may never revisit ever again due to their lack of decent portions of their bowls and the overall presentation of their meals. I'm already hungry after writing this review and I was just visiting with their location not that long ago - LOL. Their super sweet Moroccan green tea is great, but honestly, I can make that at home (Atay Bi Nana).
We don't have that many Moroccan food choices in Houston, I wish Zoa could do a bit better. Probably won't revisit this location ever again as mentioned. Until next time!”

itemListElement.name: Adair Kitchen Houston Food Review - Best Dishes To Try: Hummus, Grilled Chicken, Basque Cheesecake
itemListElement.description:
Looking for what to order at Adair Kitchen in Houston? We met up with a friend for an EatDrinkHTX dinner and tried a full spread—fresh, bright flavors with a few rich, smoky surprises.

What we ordered + flavor notes:
🥙 Hummus + roasted wild mushrooms — creamy hummus with earthy, savory mushrooms. The garlic tahini adds a bold, nutty punch, and the pomegranate brings a sweet-tart pop that cuts through the richness. Served with grilled bread.

🥪 Veggie Stack Sandwich — super flavorful and herby: grilled zucchini, roasted peppers, and mushrooms tossed in pesto (garlicky + basil-forward), with peppery arugula and red onion for crunch. Melted Swiss makes it smooth and creamy, all on toasted sourdough. Comes with house chips.

🍗 Grilled Half Chicken with salsa macha — juicy, char-grilled chicken topped with salsa macha (smoky, spicy, and a little nutty/roasty). The cilantro rice keeps it fresh and bright, and pickled onions add that tangy bite.

🌯 Simple Green Chicken Enchiladas — comforting and savory with a fresh, slightly tangy green sauce. Tender chicken, creamy refried black beans, cilantro rice, and avocado make it rich but still balanced.

🍰 Basque Cheesecake — caramelized top with a creamy center. The orange marmalade adds citrus sweetness, toasted hazelnuts give crunch, and the brown butter + sea salt brings a warm, salty-sweet finish.

Save this for your next Houston restaurant visit—especially if you’re eating at Adair Kitchen (San Felipe).
